narrative.headline: 2019 VW Jetta: powertrain, electrical, and engine drive the complaints
narrative.summary: Owners filed 533 complaints to NHTSA on the 2019 Jetta, and three areas dominate: Power Train (161 reports, 30%), Electrical System (148, 28%), and Engine (144, 27%) together account for the large majority. Engine complaints include 2 reports of fire and 4 of crashes; most areas also list a handful of injuries. Service Brakes (27) and Exterior Lighting (26) round out the list at 5% each. Read each area below for what to watch.

issues.title: Power Train
issues.blurb: The single most reported area: 161 complaints (30% of all reports), with 3 crashes and 5 injuries. The most common in this group. Worth a careful test drive and inspection.

issues.title: Electrical System
issues.blurb: A close second: 148 complaints (28%), tied to 2 crashes and 6 injuries, the most injuries of any area. Don't ignore electrical warning signs on a test drive.

issues.title: Engine
issues.blurb: 144 complaints (27%), and the only area with reported fires: 2 fires, plus 4 crashes and 4 injuries. The most safety-serious group, even if not the most reported. Take it seriously.

issues.title: Service Brakes
issues.blurb: Far fewer reports (27, 5%), but they carry weight: 4 crashes and 5 injuries from a small group. Confirm braking feels firm and responsive.

issues.title: Exterior Lighting
issues.blurb: The smallest area: 26 complaints (5%), 1 injury, with no crashes or fires reported. Mostly a check-the-lights-work item.
